main_text.l: bis expectandum fuisse, quàm tempora Ethnicorum, impleta forent, docetur & in Esaja: postquam enim dixisset Dominus egressurum furculum ex radicibus Isai, qui futurus esset vexillum populorum, quodque eum gentes requirerent, subdit de ultima Iudæorum vocatione. In die illa adijciet Dominus, secundò mittere manum suam, ad possidendum reliquum populi sui, quod remanebit ab Assur & ab Ægypto, & à Pathros, & à Chus, & ab Elam, & à Sinar, & ab Hamath, & ab Insulis maris. Et elevabit vexillum in nationibus, congregabitque profugos Israel, qui ex captivitate Thiglatpilasser & Salmanasser reliqui, in hunc usque diem, in obscuris ultimæ Asiæ locis fugitivi latent: & dispersas, postremò subversam Ierusalem, Iehudæorum animas, congregabit. Ubi & illud observandum venit, hunc ordinem in conversione Iudæorum futurum, ut primum decem tribus ab Assyrijs abductæ, ad Messiam se applicaturæ sint, quibus deinceps Iehuda & Benjamin jungetur: qua de causa hæc Israelis liberatio, Magnus dies Iezreel seu decem tribuum captivarum, apud Hoseam nuncupatur: quod

page.notes: The right margin notes are printed in italic: "Esaj. 11." and "Hof. 1. 11.", the second with an abbreviation mark. The word "quod" at the foot is the catchword and is also the first word of the next page. I was unsure of the accents on "à" (Pathros, Chus, Sinar), on "postremò" and on "secundò"; I copied them as they appear on the scan. The final line "L 2 quod" was split into signature and catchword. The note "Hof. 1. 11." sits beside the line "qua de", but its exact placement is uncertain.
